input:
## Basis
This report sets out the design of a spray dryer that dries a liquid feed to produce a powder product. The design throughput of the unit is 9 t per day of feed. The separation duty that is required is the removal of 93% of the key component from the feed, and the dried product is specified on the basis of this removal, in the sense that the product which leaves the dryer contains the balance of the key component that has not been removed. All wetted parts are manufactured in 316L stainless steel, and it is appropriate to state the grade once, at this point; the materials section of the report proceeds on the basis of this statement. The feed is a liquid which is capable of being pumped and atomised, and the design assumes that the feed is delivered to the battery limit of the dryer at the rate that has been stated. Operation is continuous at the design throughput, and the dryer is sized for that rate rather than for some form of campaign average. The drying gas is heated before it is admitted to the chamber, and the exhaust gas leaves the chamber together with the component that has been removed. The basis therefore establishes the duty and the rate, while matters such as the geometry of the chamber, the type of atomiser and the gas rate are dealt with in the sizing section.
## Sizing
The sizing starts from the two figures established in the basis, namely the design throughput of 9 t per day and the removal duty of 93% of the key component. The evaporation load follows directly from the duty, since the key component that is removed from the feed leaves the unit in the exhaust gas, and the gas rate is chosen in such a way as to carry this load while at the same time maintaining the outlet condition that is required by the product specification. The chamber itself is sized on the basis of the drying time of the droplets. The process of atomisation determines the size of the droplets, and the size of the droplets determines the length of time that each droplet requires in the hot gas in order to dry to the product condition; the volume of the chamber provides the droplets with this time at the design gas rate, with the margin being held in the height of the chamber rather than in a higher temperature of the gas. The atomiser is selected with reference to the feed as delivered: the feed is pumped to the atomiser at the design rate, and the atomiser must be capable of maintaining its droplet size over the operating range of the dryer. Product recovery forms an integral part of the sizing, in that the dried powder leaves the chamber together with the exhaust gas and is separated from the gas in the recovery step, which is sized for the full solids load at the design throughput. The heater is sized on the gas rate and on the temperature rise that the gas requires before it enters the chamber, and the pressure drop through the chamber, the recovery step and the connecting ducting determines the duty of the fan. The sizing concludes with a check of the whole train at the design rate.
## Materials
All wetted parts are manufactured in the stainless steel grade that has been named in the basis. The chamber, the body of the atomiser, the feed pipework and pump, the product outlet and the recovery equipment are all in contact with the feed, with the wet product or with the exhaust gas, and the grade applies to each and every one of them. The feed represents the most aggressive stream in the train: it wets the atomiser and the feed line on a continuous basis, and deposits derived from it find their way onto the wall of the chamber. The atomiser is subject to the hardest service, because the feed passes through it at considerable speed and any erosion that takes place there will alter the droplet size on which the sizing is based; for this reason the atomiser parts that are in the feed stream are treated as wearing parts and are designed to be replaceable. Product contact surfaces are finished smooth, in order that powder should not lodge in crevices and in order that cleaning should reach every surface with which the product comes into contact. Surfaces that are exposed only to dry gas are nevertheless held to the same grade in cases where condensate from the exhaust can form, because the exhaust gas carries the removed component and condensate derived from it cannot be regarded as clean water. Gaskets and seals are selected for the feed and for the cleaning fluids, and no gasket material is transferred from a different service without a suitable check being carried out.
## Risks
Two items remain open in the design at the present stage, namely fouling and turndown, and neither is resolved in this report. Fouling manifests itself at two places within the unit. In the first place, deposits build up on the wall of the chamber wherever droplets reach the wall before they have dried, and a fouled wall tends to shed lumps into the product as well as altering the flow of gas within the chamber; in the second place, deposits also build up at the atomiser, where even a small change in the atomising surface will alter the droplet size and, with it, the drying performance that the chamber was sized to deliver. The design provides cleaning access at the chamber and at the atomiser, and the cleaning interval is left to operating experience, since the deposit rate of the feed as delivered is not known at the design stage. Turndown constitutes the second open item. At rates below the design throughput, the atomiser has to maintain its droplet size on a reduced flow of feed, and it is by no means the case that all atomisers maintain droplet size as the flow is reduced; the gas rate falls together with the feed, the drying time of the droplets in the chamber becomes longer, and the product condition is maintained by the outlet temperature control operating over a narrower range. Both items are recorded in this report for attention at the next design stage.

Wetted parts are the stainless steel grade named in the basis. The chamber, the atomiser body, the feed pipework and pump, the product outlet and the recovery equipment all stand in contact with the feed, the wet product or the exhaust gas, and the grade is applied to each of them. The report records both items for the next design stage: the fouling item closes when a deposit rate for the feed is available, and the turndown item closes when the atomiser behaviour at reduced flow is confirmed by test.
